scenes.headline: Reading Data
scenes.subtitle: Loading files from storage into DataFrames.
scenes.narration: Reading data brings files from storage such as S3 or HDFS into Spark as a DataFrame you can process.

scenes.headline: The reader API
items: spark.read is the entry point for all formats
Supports CSV, JSON, Parquet, ORC, and more
Options control headers, schema, and delimiters
Reading is lazy — it defines the source, not the work
scenes.narration: The spark.read object is the entry point for every format, including CSV, JSON, and Parquet. Options control things like headers and schema inference, and reading is lazy: it defines the source rather than doing the work.

scenes.headline: Reading a CSV with options
scenes.narration: We build a reader, set header to true so the first row becomes column names, and enable inferSchema so Spark detects types by sampling the data. We load the CSV and call printSchema to confirm the columns and types were read correctly.

scenes.headline: Two common formats
scenes.narration: CSV and JSON are human-readable and easy to exchange, but schemas are often inferred. Parquet is columnar and compressed with the schema stored inside, making it far faster for analytics workloads.

scenes.text: Prefer Parquet for large data — inferring CSV schemas scans the file and slows reads.
scenes.narration: For large datasets prefer Parquet, since inferring a CSV schema forces Spark to scan the file and slows the read down.
